candidates.tagline: In 2018, Tesla launched this exact Roadster to space. The next-gen still can't ship.
candidates.story: Tesla announced its second-generation Roadster in November 2017, collected $250 million in deposits at up to $250,000 per reservation, promised delivery by 2020, and this week set October 1 as the fifth 'reveal event' date of 2026 alone — with production still 12–18 months away from wherever the reveal lands.
candidates.why_funny: The original Roadster went to space in 2018; nine years later, deposit-holders are still waiting for the next-gen one to reach their driveway.
candidates.alt: Elon Musk's red Tesla Roadster floating in space above Earth with a space-suited mannequin in the driver's seat, photographed from the SpaceX Falcon Heavy payload bay in February 2018

candidates.tagline: New Apple Watch records ambient conversations. In 11 states, that might be illegal.
candidates.story: Apple's Watch Series 12 (announced September 9, 2026) includes 'Live Rewind' — an always-on feature that processes the last 15 seconds of nearby audio and can replay it as text; lawyers in 11 US states with all-party consent laws say that a watch beeping at bystanders does not constitute consent to be recorded.
candidates.why_funny: Apple spent years building trust as a privacy company, then shipped a wearable that continuously listens to everyone in the room and decided a beep is a legally sufficient substitute for asking.
candidates.alt: An Apple Watch Series 12 shown on a wrist, illustrating the new always-listening Audio Intelligence feature that processes ambient conversations and may raise eavesdropping concerns under US state wiretapping laws
